info.title: SlideForge API
info.description: Agent-first PowerPoint generation. Send structured slide intents (a `form` plus typed fields) or a brief; get back a real, editable `.pptx`. The draw path is deterministic — no model renders your slide, so supplied numbers and text come out verbatim. Every response carries `status`, `fidelity` and `warnings` so an automated caller can tell whether the output is usable. $0.05 per slide; an unusable slide is not billed. Authenticate with a SlideForge API key (`Authorization: Bearer sf_live_…` or `X-API-Key`) — new accounts include 60 free slides, no credit card: https://slideforge.dev/sign-up

post.description: The public half of /tools/pdf-to-pptx: returns producer, page count, source classification and `can_extract` so a visitor learns whether their PDF converts to editable shapes — before signing up. No job, no persistence, no conversion, no charge. Converting is authenticated: POST /v1/deck/from-pdf.

post.summary: Run python-pptx code and return a preview image (public, no auth)
post.description: Executes python-pptx code in the sandbox and returns slide 1 as an inline PNG (768px) plus static lint findings (overlaps, off-canvas shapes, tiny fonts, chart semantics) in `lint[]`. Send a python-pptx script as it is (the presentation it saves is the one shown), or a `build(prs)` function. No .pptx is produced and nothing is downloadable — the file, PDF export, and full-resolution renders live in the playground and /v1/render/code. 16KB code cap, 10s timeout, 1 slide.

post.description:
RFC 7591 - Dynamic Client Registration.

Redirect URIs are validated to prevent open-redirect attacks:
- HTTPS, loopback HTTP, or a private-use native-app scheme (RFC 8252 §7.1:
  cursor://, windsurf://, ...). Plain http:// to a real host stays rejected
  (cleartext), as do browser-executable schemes. PKCE — S256, enforced
  unconditionally at /oauth/authorize — is what makes custom schemes safe:
  an app that hijacks the scheme catches the code but cannot exchange it
  without the verifier. ADR-2026-08-16-dcr-custom-scheme-redirects.

Cap of 100 registered clients enforced via LRU eviction (oldest by
last_used_at) — friendlier than 503 for legitimate clients while
bounding storage growth.

get.description: OAuth 2.1 Authorization endpoint - redirects to Auth0 with PKCE.
OAuth callback - receives Auth0 code, redirects back to MCP client.

post.description:
RFC 7009 token revocation — ADR-2026-08-01 clause 5.

Proxies revocation to Auth0 and drops our matching grant rows. This is what lets a client's
"disconnect" actually kill the long-lived credential rather than merely forgetting it.

Bounded on purpose: revoking a refresh token does NOT end the session. The outstanding access
token stays valid until `exp` (24h in prod) plus up to 30 min of middleware token cache. That
bound exists today for every access token; this endpoint does not widen it and does not claim
to close it.

Per RFC 7009 §2.2 an unknown or already-revoked token is a SUCCESS, not an error — otherwise
the endpoint becomes a token-validity oracle.
OAuth 2.1 Token endpoint - exchanges code for access token.

RFC 8058 one-click. The mail client posts here with no human present.

The token travels in the query string — that is what the List-Unsubscribe header carries.
The POST body is the fixed `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` and is not read.

get.description: The link in the body, clicked by a person.

post.description:
Stamp the first click on a campaign mail. Called by the web middleware, not a person.

Campaign links are ordinary slideforge.dev URLs carrying `?src=&sid=`; Resend's own click
tracking, which would rewrite every link through a tracking subdomain, stays off. So the
click reaches us the same way any other visit does and this endpoint is what turns a
landing into an attributed click.

Unauthenticated for the same reason unsubscribe is: the reader has usually not logged in
yet — /console/billing, where the top-up mails point, bounces them through Auth0 first.
A `sid` grants nothing; the only effect it can have is setting one timestamp on the row
it names, once.

Silent on an unknown id. The middleware fires this without waiting for the answer, so a
404 would be read by nobody and would only tell a prober which ids exist.

post.description: Brief → SSG intent route → deterministic render. The brief path used by MCP `create_slide` when only a prose brief is supplied. $0.05 per slide. Unroutable briefs return a 422 `intent_unroutable` error with no charge. Explicit style asks in the brief (dark/light, corporate/technical/... looks) map onto built-in themes automatically unless `theme_id` is set; the response names the mapping and any unsupported styling.

post.summary: Render a slide from a structured SSG intent (mirrors MCP create_slide)
post.description:
Deterministic SSG render from a structured intent — the REST mirror of the MCP create_slide tool. Provide ONE of: `form` (+ typed content fields) for a typed intent, `prior_id` (+`content`) to render an exact catalog prior (no routing), `author_ssg` for a full AuthorSSG document, or a prose `brief`. $0.05 per slide.

`preview:true` → a FREE ephemeral PNG preview (no job, no charge, nothing downloadable). Eligible only for verbatim inputs (`prior_id`/`author_ssg`); briefs/images return 400 (use Generate).

Brief-mode style asks (dark/light, look adjectives) auto-map onto built-in themes unless `theme_id` is set — pick one explicitly via GET /v1/brands or browse_catalog(type=themes).

post.description:
Run full vision perception (4 parallel vision-model specialists) and
return a SlideIntentIR structured spec. Phase 2 of the
Perception → Planner v2 plan.

Bills `image_analysis_v2` ($0.20) on success only. The returned
`SlideIntentIR` is the input the Planner v2 will consume (P4).
Today, callers can also drive it through the legacy auto-router by
extracting `brief = perception.brief()` (helper TBD).

INTERNAL ENDPOINT — perception schema is IP-load-bearing and not
advertised in the public MCP surface. Keep on this REST path until
we decide otherwise.

post.summary: Estimate cost+duration before running full image analysis
post.description:
Run a single cheap vision pass to estimate the cost+duration of the
full from-image flow. Free to the user; we eat ~$0.02/call internally.

The frontend uses this output to render a "Will cost $X-Y, balance $Z.
Proceed?" confirmation before committing to the expensive perception
path. Auto-mode can skip the confirmation; customize-mode shows
per-asset choices once we have asset-level data (P2).

Analyze an uploaded image and return a synthesized slide brief.

Sync. Bills `image_analysis` ($0.05) on success only. Feed the returned
`brief` into POST /v1/render/auto to produce a slide.

For multi-slide breakdowns (`slide_count > 1`) returns
`AnalyzeImageMultiResponse` with one entry per slide; the agent then
calls /v1/render/auto once per slide and assembles a deck.

post.description:
Upload a .pptx file and receive a translated version with all formatting preserved. Runs asynchronously — the response contains a job_id to poll via GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}.

**Max file size:** 50 MB.  **Max slides:** 100.  **Macros rejected.**

**Pricing:** $0.02 per slide, flat. The wallet is checked for every slide before any work starts (402 with a checkout link if it cannot cover the deck); slides whose translation still overflows at the minimum font size are not billed.

**Fidelity-preserving:** text runs are translated in place via python-pptx, preserving fonts, colors, sizes, positions, charts, tables, and embedded images.

Identical pricing and identical background pipeline as /v1/translate; the only difference is the request shape.

post.summary: Inspect any PPTX — read-only Deck Quality Report (free)
post.description: Structural quality report for ANY deck — a prior SlideForge job, an https URL, or uploaded bytes. Deterministic checks (no LLM): clipped/overflowing text via real font metrics, tiny fonts, off-canvas objects, text collisions, WCAG contrast, image-only slides — with honest coverage for what inherited theme formatting hides. Free; ≤25 MB; first 50 slides.

200.description: The Deck Quality Report (status: clean | review | failed)

post.summary: Repair a PPTX deterministically — sizes, colors, invisible junk; never your words ($0.02/repaired slide)
post.description: Applies deterministic fixes to inspect findings: shrink_to_fit (real font metrics, floor 9pt), raise_min_font (only when the box still fits), remove_off_canvas (fully-invisible parked shapes), fix_contrast (WCAG, hue-preserving). No characters are ever altered — the response carries a computed visible_text_untouched proof. Ambiguous defects are flagged, never guessed. $0.02 per repaired slide (a slide with ≥1 fix); dry_run plans the exact fixes for FREE; no_changes never bills. ≤25 MB; first 50 slides.

Currently supports PDFs exported from slide tools (PowerPoint, Keynote, Google Slides, Canva, LaTeX Beamer, etc.). Text documents are not converted: to turn a document into slides, let the calling assistant read it and send the slides as intents.

**Max file size:** 50 MB.

post.description:
Accept a PPTX from the MCP Apps iframe, kick off translation.

Token is minted by `upload_asset(purpose="translate", target_language=...)`.
Target language is carried in the token's signed payload — the iframe
doesn't need to pass it on the upload. Reuses the existing
`translate_upload` worker (same endpoint `/v1/translate` serves web form).

Returns `{job_id, poll_url}` once the job is created; iframe polls
`/v1/jobs/{id}` for completion. No server-side chain (translate is
the final step).

Accept a brand template PPTX from the MCP Apps drop-zone, extract the theme.

Token is minted by `upload_asset(purpose="theme")` with no inline data. Unlike pdf/translate
there is NO job to poll — extraction is synchronous and the response carries `theme_id`; the
result card renders a success panel (U4 ADR §7.4: renders on this theme are NATIVE by default,
built on the uploaded file).

Accept a PDF from the MCP Apps iframe, kick off conversion.

Returns `{job_id, status: "queued", poll_url}` immediately. The
iframe polls the signed poll_url against `/v1/jobs/{job_id}` for
completion, then transitions the result card to the populated state.

Auth: `X-Upload-Token` header (minted by `upload_asset(purpose="pdf")`).
No Bearer token; the upload token carries the user identity.

Accept a slide image from the MCP Apps iframe, recreate it as an
editable slide (ADR 2026-08-05 recreate). Returns `{job_id, poll_url}`
immediately; the pipeline runs as a background task and the iframe polls
the signed route — the pdf async shape.

Record a UI interaction event tied to a specific job.

Auth by signed URL (`sig` + `exp`). No Bearer token required — the

Slide 2 (optional): Velocity & throughput trend chart + 3-5 explanatory bullets.

**Audience:** executives, sponsors, steering committees.
**Cadence:** weekly or per-sprint.
**Scope:** project (with project_id) or workspace-wide.

**Modes:** `connection_id` (we fetch from Zoho) or `prepared_data` (SprintMetrics-shaped dict). Pricing $0.06 per report (2 × $0.03).

1. Executive Dashboard (6 KPIs)
2. Sprint Burndown (ideal-line dashed + actual line — research convention)
3. Velocity History (last N sprints + 3-sprint rolling average overlay)
4. Completed Work (closed items, epic-grouped)
5. Rollover (items still in flight at sprint end)
6. Highlights & Risks (auto-detected signals)

**Audience:** PO, team, stakeholders.
**Cadence:** end of every sprint.
**Scope:** project (with project_id) or workspace-wide.

**Modes:** `connection_id` or `prepared_data`. Pricing $0.18 (6 × $0.03).

**Audience:** RTE, Product Mgmt, executives.

Surfaced on JobStatus.quality_warnings. Non-blocking — the job status
stays `complete`/`partial`; quality_warnings is a separate signal an
agent can read to decide whether to iterate.

severity:
  - 'bug'        — real visual issue (text overlap, off-canvas, contrast
                   fail, font outside legible range). MCP card surfaces
                   a banner when any 'bug' entries exist.
  - 'suggestion' — soft hint (high shape count, missing title zone,
                   borderline font). Silent in the MCP card.

source:
  - 'static_linter' — convergence/linter.py output (3.2a)
  - 'vlm'           — Pixtral one-shot review (3.2b, future)
  - 'report_linter' — convergence/quality/report_linter.py output

quality_profile.title: Quality Profile
quality_profile.description: Readiness thresholds the layout block is judged against: executive | technical (default) | appendix.

fail_on_vlm.title: Fail On Vlm
fail_on_vlm.description: VLM finding categories that BLOCK (escalate to errors, render free per usable-or-free): substring match on the finding, e.g. ['contrast', 'clipping']. A high-confidence `overlap` and any `content_missing` already block by default. Requires verify=lint+vlm.

content.title: Content
content.description: Typed business facts (ADR 2026-07-14): available read-only as CONTENT inside the code; the renderer verifies every leaf rendered verbatim and emits fidelity + provenance. Keys named 'id' are references, not display content.

code_profile.title: Code Profile
code_profile.description: widgets_only = compose via add_widget + approved helpers + CONTENT/theme only; raw python-pptx (slide.shapes.*, add_text_box/add_box, add_slide) is rejected. Omit or 'native' for full access. Response echoes code_profile.applied + violations.

patch.title: Patch
patch.description: the slide fields to change (same fields as create_slide). A field left out keeps its value, a field sent as null is removed, a list replaces the whole list, `data` merges key by key. Send only `notes` to add or replace speaker notes without a re-render.

SlideReplacement.title: SlideReplacement
SlideReplacement.description: One slide to swap in a deck.

SlideSpec.title: SlideSpec
SlideSpec.description: One slide within a deck request.

ToolAttempt.title: ToolAttempt
ToolAttempt.description: A file picked on a free-tool page. Shape only — never a filename or content.

TranslateFromJobRequest.title: TranslateFromJobRequest
TranslateFromJobRequest.description:
POST /v1/translate/from-job request body.

JSON-body alternative to /v1/translate (multipart) for the no-file case.
Cleaner DX for agents that don't want to construct multipart for what is
effectively a JSON request: 'translate this existing job into German'.

VariantPreviewRequest.title: VariantPreviewRequest
VariantPreviewRequest.description: A pinned catalog variant to render. NOT a brief — see the endpoint docstring.

url.title: Url
url.description: HTTPS endpoint URL to receive events

events.title: Events
events.description: Event types to subscribe to (default: all)

bearerAuth.description: SlideForge API key: `Authorization: Bearer sf_live_…`. Create one at https://slideforge.dev/console/keys

apiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
apiKeyAuth.description: Same key, header form — for clients that cannot set Authorization.
